reasoning.Student A:
The key property says the set of schools you can possibly be matched with (the Obtainable Schools) is fixed regardless of how you rank them. Your submitted ranking only chooses which school you get among that fixed set — you receive the highest-ranked school (in your submitted list) that lies in the Obtainable Schools. Therefore you cannot use your ranking to expand or shift the attainable set; the only sensible goal is to ensure that, whatever the obtainable set turns out to be, the school you most prefer among those is listed highest.

Given that, the optimal strategy is to rank sincerely according to your true preferences: put y first (you prefer y most and have priority 1 there), then x, then z, then w. This guarantees that if y is obtainable you get it; if not but x is obtainable you get x; and so on. Trying to manipulate the order cannot make an unreachable school obtainable.
reasoning.Student B:
Given the mechanism's key property, the set of schools I could possibly be matched with (my Obtainable Schools) is fixed by others' rankings and schools' priorities and cannot be changed by how I rank. My submitted ranking therefore cannot make an unattainable school obtainable; it only determines which school I receive inside that fixed set (I get the highest-ranked school among the obtainable ones).

Because of that, the dominant strategy is to list my true preferences so that, whatever the obtainable set is, I receive the most-preferred school within it. My true preference ordering is y > x > z > w. Note also my priority: x and z are higher priority for me (rank 1) while y and w are rank 2, but since the obtainable set is fixed, this only affects which schools are in that set and not how I should order them. Therefore I should rank sincerely: y first, then x, then z, then w.

Therefore the dominant strategy is to list my true preferences so that, once the mechanism chooses among the obtainable schools, I get the best one for me.

Given my true tastes (y > x > z > w) and the priorities, I should rank schools in that true order. The fact that most applicants favor y > x > w > z and that my priorities at y and z are lower doesn't change this conclusion: it may affect which schools are in my obtainable set, but it is not something I can influence by misranking. So I report my genuine preference order.
